payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated the thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery, designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and associated aging. Its governing corrected cycle life is 8,400, replacing the retracted 12,000-cycle press-release claim. The prototype’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, while projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte below that temperature.

FLAGS: Source C reports both “4,800 cycles” measured to the 80% knee and “8,400 cycles” as the corrected governing figure.
VERDICT: APPROVE

The Brennecke Institute originated the thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery, designed to reduce electrolyte crossover. Its corrected cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the governing 80% capacity threshold; the earlier 12,000 claim was retracted after independent audit. The cell has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg, a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh scale, and an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that temperature.

FLAGS: Source C conflicts internally: it reports “4,800 cycles” to the 80% capacity knee but also says “8,400 cycles” is the corrected governing figure.
VERDICT: APPROVE
